objective: At the owner's go-ahead ("Yes, let's continue") on direction 1 of TOY-PHASE-20261127-001: declare, as a scaffold, which values commute, decided at the end of the round in which the later of two distinctions is born and never revised, with the sign of each implied birth forced by the cost of reordering. The local rule lets two values fail to commute only if one of them is already held twice. Prove it keeps a state at every round; then, on every census start grown up to four rounds, ask at each closure whether the local rule can make the close odd, against the whole-structure reading of NO-WHOLE-STATE (odd attainable exactly where the pattern is not outerplanar), and where the natural local rule (every locally decidable unheld pair fails to commute) loses its state. G18 Comparing growth laws. Stop when every frozen prediction is scored.

title: Commutation fixed at birth: can growth's own closures still close odd?
